summary: JClaw enforces architecture as ordinary tests over bytecode: strict ArchUnit rules where the codebase is clean, FreezingArchRules with committed named stores where it is not (store creation AND update pinned off, so a stale entry fails until deleted by hand), a live-match floor beside every frozen rule so a predicate that stops matching cannot pass vacuously, and 'gate conformance' tests that read the gate's own configuration and fail on known switch-offs. Two seams back this: AppClock (one wall-clock reader, ScopedValue-bound in tests) and TaskScope (fan-out that cancels siblings on first failure). Property tests are jqwik, tries pinned with a wall-time comment, generated input in every failure message. OUR STATE: we already HAVE the frozen-store idea (tests/game-purity-ratchet.test.ts, per-file value multisets, env-var refresh with a RED receipt), vacuity floors (claimcheck >1600/>350, chaos 43, twins 36), stale-exception checks (claimcheck STALE-CONTEXT) and fail-closed discovery. The real gaps are narrower: (1) our ratchet lets a removed literal leave a ghost cap that a later re-add slips under (0 ghosts measured today, so latent); (2) nothing reads .githooks/pre-commit, tsconfig.json or eslint.config.mjs, so an emptied TEST_CMD or a flipped strict flag is silent; (3) the core/CLAUDE.md bans on Math.random/Date.now are prose only, and that file already carries two claims the scanner contradicts (implicit enum ordinals ARE caught; Infinity is used 5x while 'banned by intent'); (4) no property-style per-frame invariant sweep exists. Verdicts: ADOPT the scanner-enforced clock/randomness ban; ADAPT the stale-cap check, the gate-conformance test, a hand-rolled seeded invariant sweep, and a per-file config-label gate; SKIP TaskScope semantics and the things we already have. Do NOT copy: signature+line-number store entries (churn), properties-file flip regeneration with no receipt, rule prose duplicated in an 887-line AGENTS.md, gates in pre-push with a skip env var.

candidates.pattern: Gate-conformance test: a test that reads the gate's OWN configuration (build file, hook, compiler flags), strips comments first, and fails on the known ways of switching the gate off or downgrading it — so disarming a gate is itself a red test, not a later discovery.
candidates.failurePrevented: A pre-commit hook with TEST_CMD emptied (the hook's own contract: `[ -z "$2" ] && return 0` skips silently), `npm run chaos` added to pre-commit (it rewrites shipped source), tsconfig `strict`/`noUncheckedIndexedAccess` flipped, eslint dropping strictTypeChecked, or vitest `include` narrowed — each of which leaves every existing test green while the gate checks less.

Commit 3c498c7b: adding a parameter "added the model-override env and args to runAcpBatch ... the frozen store matches on the parameter list, so the six SubagentAcpRunner entries stopped matching" → 6 lines hand-rewritten with no new holder. Commit 245ddc1f: "the diff is the new rule descriptions in stored.rules and line renumbering."
antiPatterns.whyNotForUs: Our baseline is a per-file value MULTISET with no line numbers (tests/game-purity-ratchet.test.ts:3-4, tests/game-purity-baseline.json), so a refactor that moves a literal within a file changes nothing — keep that.
